author.department: Department of Mathematics and Computer Science

introduction.p: This is a literate programming version of the RELAX-NG schema for 's Pulbication Files. It is based on the corresponding version for 's RELAX-NG schema written by Rob Beezer. It is used to generate the RELAX-NG compact syntax version (pretext.rnc) and other versions are derived from the compact version with standard tools.

The main use for this schema currently is to let publishers more easily write publication files for projects since the pretext-tools extension for VS Code uses (the derived version) of this schema to provide completions and (eventually) validation.
Comments in this file are kept to a minimum. Full documentation of publisher options are presented in the guide.
More information about how RELAX-NG schemas work, as well as how the literate programming version of this schema works, can be found in the schema.

section.title: Start Element
section.p: The only start element for a publication file is publication.

section.title: Gross Structure
section.p: A publication file always has the root element publication. After that, all elements are optional. Those elements include common options, and options for numbering, latex, html, reveal.js, epub, braille, source, and . These can come in any order.

fragment.title: Gross structure
fragment.code: Publication = element publication { Common? & Source? & Numbering? & Latex? & Pdf? & Html? & Revealjs? & Beamer? & Epub? & Jupyter? & Braille? & Text? & Webwork? & Dynamics? }

section.title: Numbering Options
section.p: These options will affect multiplt output formats, all related to numbering.

The distinct switch on projects, figures, exercises, and openproblems determines whether those blocks run on their own counter (distinct="yes", at the given level) or share the overall blocks counter (distinct="no", the default).

section.title: Braille Options
section.p: These option(s) control the braille output. The page geometry describes an embossed page: the number of cells in a line, and the number of lines on a page. The default geometry is 40 cells by 25 lines, a common size for North American embossers.

section.title: Text Options
section.p: These option(s) control the plain text and markdown outputs. The character repertoire is unicode (the default) for genuine dashes, quotations marks, and the like, or ascii for stand-ins drawn from the 7-bit repertoire.

section.title: Dynamic Exercise Options
section.p: A fill-in-the-blank exercise may generate its content with Javascript, and may import a library to do so. In HTML that library runs in the reader's browser, sandboxed as any web page is. A static conversion has no browser, so the same library is instead run once at build time, under Node, with the privileges of whoever is building the book.

That difference is why a library named by a url has to be approved here before a static build will run it. Approval is per-library rather than a blanket switch, so approving one library never extends to a different one an exercise imports later. A library kept with the project needs no approval, since it is already the author's own code. HTML is not gated at all.

Only a secure URL may be approved. The extraction script refuses any other scheme outright, before approval is ever consulted, so an entry naming one could never match and would sit here as dead configuration.

fragment.title: Dynamic Exercise Options

section.title: Hierarchical Structure
section.p: We collect all the specifications, roughly in a top-down order, so the generated schema files have a rational ordering to them, even if the order presented here is different.
